title: Charity
tomorrow: the "blessed are" lines: whose portrait are they?

lines: A LIST OF THINGS LOVE DOES.
cards: Love on an ordinary Tuesday doesn't look like a movie. It looks like a roommate who leaves the last of the coffee for you. A coworker who covers your shift without telling the whole office.

A sister who listens to the same worry a third time. None of it would make a highlight reel. Paul, writing to a church in Corinth that was arguing about almost everything, gives the word for this a list.
And when you look closely, every item on it is something love does.

teach.b: Here's the start of the list, in the Douay-Rheims: "Charity is patient, is kind: charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely; is not puffed up." Charity is the older English for this love, from the Latin caritas.
Today the word can sound like a donation box. Paul means something bigger and more daily.
The Catechism calls charity the virtue by which we love God above all things, and our neighbor as ourselves, for the love of God. Two directions, one love.

teach.h: LOVE GOD, HATE YOUR BROTHER? NO.
teach.b: And the first letter of John won't let them come apart: "If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar." That's blunt, and it's the point. In Paul's list, love isn't a mood that comes and goes.
It's patient when the line is long. Kind when nobody is watching. Not keeping score.

teach.h: LOVE IS A VERB IN PAUL'S GREEK.
teach.b: Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in Paul's Greek, love is patient isn't an adjective.
It's a verb, something love keeps doing. So the question for a Tuesday isn't do I feel loving. It's what does patience, or kindness, look like with this person, today.
That's why Catholics call it an act of love. Not a feeling you wait for. A thing you do.

how: Catholics name charity as the greatest of the three theological virtues; some pray a short traditional Act of Love, and many hear 1 Corinthians 13 read at weddings.

o: a warm feeling toward people you like
the love that loves God and neighbor together
money or goods given to people in need

games.q: what love does — tap the pairs.
p: love God, hate your brother: a lie

s: charity in the Bible mostly means giving money to the poor
Paul's charity is the love that loves God and neighbor together; giving is one way it shows.
the first letter of John says you can't love God and hate your brother
"If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar."
for Catholics, love is a feeling you wait for
the Catechism calls charity a virtue, and Paul's list is made of things love does.

games.q: your grandpa tells the same story at every dinner, and your cousins roll their eyes. he starts it again. what does Paul's list point to?
o: gently remind him he's told it before.
listen as if it's new; charity is patient, is kind.
slip away; love doesn't mean being bored.
games.why: Paul's list starts with patient and kind, and both are things love does, not feelings it waits for. the correction is true; the patience is love.

practice: Choose one person you'll see in the next day. Name what you'd like to give them, one patient or kind thing; then the thing most likely to get in the way, like being tired, or rushed, or still annoyed.
Decide now what you'll do when that obstacle shows up, and rest in the plan.

wordCard.voice: Charity. Not a donation box: the love that loves God and neighbor together, patient and kind on an ordinary day.

orig.note: Greek: love. the word Paul uses all through 1 Corinthians 13, rendered charity in the Douay-Rheims.

carryVoice: Keep this one: I love, which in Paul's list is something you keep doing, not something you wait to feel. Until tomorrow.
